```{r initialize, message=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(readxl)

knit_hooks$set(inline = function(x) {
  prettyNum(x, big.mark=" ")
})

```

# Data Source

Polygenic hazard score (PHS) model summary statistics (sumstats) downloaded from the [PGS Catalog](https://www.pgscatalog.org/), PGS Publication number [PGP000047](https://www.pgscatalog.org/publication/PGP000047/) from @seibert2018.

# Pre-process sumstats

```{r import_sumstats}
sumstats = read_tsv('PGS000067_hmPOS_GRCh37.txt.gz', comment = "#")

sumstats
```

The model from @seibert2018 contains `{r} nrow(sumstats)` SNPs. The cleansumstats pipeline may not handle leading comments, so we removed them on import. Some of the extraneous columns can crash cleansumstats so we will remove them and just keep the necessary columns.

```{r drop_columns}
sumstats %>% 
  select(rsID, chr_name, chr_position,
         effect_allele, other_allele, effect_weight) ->
  sumstats
```

## Sample size

```{r cases_controls}
n_case = 18868
n_control = 12879
```

cleansumstats also requires a sample size (N, N_case, and/or N_control). The original paper uses the PRACTICAL consortium with a sample size of `{r} n_case` cases and `{r} n_control` controls [@seibert2018], so we will add those as columns.

```{r, add_n}
sumstats %>% 
  mutate(n_cases = n_case) %>% 
  mutate(n_controls = n_control) ->
  sumstats
```

## Ambiguous SNPs

```{r, ambiguous_SNPs}

get_ambiguous_snps <- function(x, A1, A2) {
  A1 = sym(A1)
  A2 = sym(A2)
  x %>% 
  filter((!!A1 %in% c('C', 'G') & !!A2 %in% c('C', 'G')) | 
           (!!A1 %in% c('A', 'T') & !!A2 %in% c('A', 'T')))
}

sumstats %>% 
  get_ambiguous_snps(A1 = 'effect_allele', A2 = 'other_allele') ->
  ambiguous_SNPs
```

The cleansumstats pipeline will remove SNPs with ambiguous base changes (i.e., A/T or C/G). Here we can see we have `{r} nrow(ambiguous_SNPs)`:

```{r}
kable(ambiguous_SNPs)
```

## Non-ACTG SNPs

We do not have any non-ACTG SNPs:

```{r nonACTG_SNPs}
sumstats %>% 
  filter(!(effect_allele %in% c('A', 'C', 'T', 'G')) |
           !(other_allele %in% c('A', 'C', 'T', 'G'))) %>% 
  kable()
```

## Missing RS numbers

```{r missing_rs}
# SNPs without an rs#
sumstats %>% 
  filter(!str_starts(rsID, 'rs') | is.na(rsID)) ->
  missing_rs

kable(missing_rs)
```

We also have `{r} nrow(missing_rs)` variants with missing RS numbers, which `cleansumstats` will add based on chromosome number and base pair position.

## Missing p-values

This model has no p-values, but PRSice requires it so we will add a new column with values of 1 for every SNP.

```{r}
sumstats$P = 1
```

Based on the above, we should expect our model returned from `cleansumstats` with `{r} nrow(sumstats) - nrow(ambiguous_SNPs)` or fewer SNPs due to ambiguous base changes.

```{r write_sumstats}
write_tsv(sumstats, 'PGS000067_hmPOS_GRCh37_cleaned.txt.gz')
```

## Metadata file

Lastly, we need a `.yaml` file with metadata for our sumstats.

```{r write_yaml}
yaml <- c(
  "cleansumstats_metafile_kind: minimal",
  "path_sumStats: PGS000067_hmPOS_GRCh37_cleaned.txt.gz",
  "stats_Model: cox",
  "col_CHR: chr_name",
  "col_POS: chr_position",
  "col_EffectAllele: effect_allele",
  "col_OtherAllele: other_allele",
  "col_BETA: effect_weight",
  "col_SNP: rsID",
  "col_CaseN: n_cases",
  "col_ControlN: n_controls",
  "col_P: P")

write_lines(yaml, "PGS000067_hmPOS_GRCh37_cleaned.yaml")
```

# Pre-process genotype and phenotype data

## Phenotype

```{r preprocess_phenotype}
allData = read_excel('FW__Poly_tables/poly_final_220425_estimated_lastobs.xls', sheet = 1)
caseData = read_excel('FW__Poly_tables/poly_final_220425_estimated_lastobs.xls', sheet = 2)

# Grab all male IDs
allData %>% 
  filter(SEX == "M") %>% 
  pull(PID) %>% 
  unique() ->
  allMaleIDs

# Grab IDs of prostate cancer cases
caseData %>% 
  filter(pid %in% allMaleIDs) %>% 
  filter(icd9 == 185) %>% 
  pull(pid) %>% 
  unique ->
prostateIDs

# Grab IDs of all cancer cases
caseData %>% 
  filter(pid %in% allMaleIDs) %>% 
  pull(pid) %>% 
  unique() ->
  caseIDs

# Grab IDs for all cancer-free males
allData %>% 
  filter(PID %in% allMaleIDs) %>% 
  filter(!(PID %in% caseIDs)) %>% 
  pull(PID) %>% 
  unique() ->
  controlIDs

# Double check no cancer cases or prostate cases are in control IDs
try(for (i in caseIDs) (if (i %in% controlIDs) stop("Found case ID in controls.")))
try(for (i in prostateIDs) (if (i %in% controlIDs) stop("Found prostate ID in controls.")))

write_lines(postateIDs, 'FW__Poly_tables/case_pids.txt')
write_lines(controlIDs, 'FW__Poly_tables/control_pids.txt')
```

# Run `cleansumstats` pipeline

Uses the [cleansumstats wrapper](https://github.com/precimed/GWAS_SUMSTAT/tree/master/JF) from Julian (and dependent on the original [cleansumstats pipeline](https://github.com/BioPsyk/cleansumstats)) available using command `run_cleansumstats.sh` on TSD p33.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
bash run_cleansumstats.sh \
  /ess/p33/cluster/users/andrewmo/PGS000067_hmPOS_GRCh37_cleaned.yaml \
  /ess/p33/cluster/users/andrewmo/sumstats/out \
  /ess/p33/cluster/users/andrewmo/scratch \
  p33
```

```{r import_cleansumstats}
cleansumstats <- read_tsv('PGS000067_hmPOS_GRCh37_cleaned.GRCh37.gz')
kable(cleansumstats)
```

## SNPs removed by `cleansumstats`

After `cleansumstats` there are `{r} nrow(cleansumstats)` SNPs left in the model and `{r} nrow(sumstats) - nrow(cleansumstats)` were removed.

Here are the SNPs that were removed:

```{r}
cleansumstats %>%
  mutate(CHR = as.character(CHR)) %>% 
  right_join(sumstats, by = c("CHR" = "chr_name", "POS" = "chr_position")) %>% 
  filter(is.na(RSID)) %>% 
  select(-(RSID:ControlN)) ->
  removed_SNPs

kable(removed_SNPs)

removed_SNPs %>% 
  get_ambiguous_snps(A1 = 'effect_allele', A2 = 'other_allele') ->
  ambiguous_snps2

removed_SNPs %>% 
  anti_join(ambiguous_snps2, by = c('CHR', 'POS')) ->
  removed_SNPs2

removed_SNPs2 %>% 
  filter(CHR == 'X') ->
  removed_Xchr

removed_SNPs2 %>% 
  anti_join(removed_Xchr, by = 'CHR') ->
  removed_SNPs3

```

It removed all `{r} nrow(ambiguous_snps2)` ambiguous snps. At also removed all `{r} nrow(removed_Xchr)` SNPs that were on the X chromosome. The last remaining SNP is:

```{r}
kable(removed_SNPs3)
```

It is unclear why `cleansumstats` removed this SNP.
